Definition: type of heterothermy as classified by the paper (printed column T): DT = daily torpor, torpor bouts lasting less than 24 h with continued foraging; HIB = hibernation, torpor bouts lasting consecutive days to weeks in animals that usually do not forage but rely on energy stores
Note: two levels only in the data: DT (119 rows) and HIB (94 rows). Species were initially assigned on TBDmax (<24 h vs >24 h) as reported by the original authors; two documented exceptions - Sminthopsis macroura kept as DT despite TBDmax 25.9 h, and Elephantulus myurus kept as DT despite 39 h. Gaussian-mixture cluster analysis in the paper supports the two categories as functionally distinct groups
Source Note: printed Table 1 column T; legend 'T, type: daily torpor (DT) or hibernation (HIB)'; classification rules in Methods sec. II, p. 893; type definitions in the Abstract, p. 891

Definition: maximum torpor bout duration (TBDmax) in hours
Note: the variable the initial DT/HIB classification was based on. Range in the data 1 to 6480 h. No value was assigned for Ursus americanus, Ursus arctos and Meles meles, whose multiday Tb cycles are not considered homologous to small-hibernator arousals
Source Note: printed Table 1 column TBDmax; legend 'TBDmax, maximum torpor bout duration (h)'; special cases in Methods sec. II, p. 893

Definition: mean torpor bout duration (TBDmean) in hours
Note: often not reported by the original study; where missing the authors either recalculated it from raw mid-hibernation figures or estimated it as the average of a printed minimum-maximum range - so this column mixes reported and reconstructed means
